title: GTA 6 Finally Changed The Default Rockstar-Game Controls
description: If you've played Rockstar series like Grand Theft Auto or Read Dead Redemption over the past few decades, then you're familiar with their default control scheme, which maps sprinting to a face button instead of the left analog stick. But Grand Theft Auto VI isn't being hailed as a revolutionary game for nothing--at long last, the default scheme has changed. As we learned while playing Grand Theft Auto VI, instead of the default setup mapping sprint to a button (A on Xbox and X on PS5), the game maps it to the left analog stick. However, you're free to switch it back to the style used in games like Red Dead Redemption 2, if you prefer. This is a very handy change, because mapping sprinting to a face button effectively stops you from being able to easily do some of your other actions, unless you have no dignity like me and will use your own face to press a button when your hands are full. The new default control scheme is far from the most impressive thing in Grand Theft Auto 6, of course. The game earned a rare 10/10 in our GTA 6 review, with Tamoor Hussain calling it "the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach." For more on the game, check out our ever-expanding GTA 6 guides hub and learn what you should do first. That shouldn't include buying a whole new pro controller, however.

title: GTA 6 Isn’t Worth Buying A Fancy Controller For
description: In all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto VI (check out our 10/10 review ), it might be tempting to upgrade your setup. For a game 13 years in the making, is now the time to upgrade my TV? Maybe a PS5 Pro is in order? It's a coincidence I finally upgraded my speaker system after 18 years, I swear. One cheaper upgrade than those above you might be considering is a better controller, like a DualSense Edge or Xbox Elite controller. For all of their myriad upgrades, the most essential reason to ever buy one of these, in my opinion, is for the back paddles. Although they are not technically extra buttons, the ability to map an inconveniently placed button to one of them can make an experience far smoother. Some games make an exceptionally strong case for only playing with paddles. You do a lot of sprinting and picking things up in Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, and having to take my thumb off the right stick (thus temporarily locking the camera in place) is something I find to be a constant annoyance. It's such an improvement to be able to do those things while keeping my thumbs where they belong. Grand Theft Auto VI, on the other hand, is not such an example. Rockstar has finally made a change to the default control scheme it uses in its games, mapping sprint to a click of the left stick, rather than the traditional usage of the X (PlayStation) and A (Xbox) buttons. That alone alleviates a potential argument for needing back paddles (at least as much as one can need such a thing). That's not to say there's literally zero use for one of these pro-style controllers in GTA 6. In our experience, tapping a paddle is arguably still an improvement to clicking the left stick to sprint or holding L1/LB to bring up the weapon wheel. Enabling Focus Mode is done by clicking both sticks, which you might find awkward; accomplishing that with paddles might be comfortable for you. GTA 6 doesn't allow its controls to be freely remapped, though there are some options available…

title: How Much Does Gas Cost In GTA 6 Vs. Real Life?
description: There are many questions swirling around the internet right now, as the global launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 begins to roll out. Who are the voice actors? How long does it take to beat GTA 6? But, perhaps most importantly, how financially screwed are you if you want to drive across Leonida rather than taking advantage of the extensive public transport network? Well, thanks to streamer AaronGameDeveloperAU, we know the answer now. Via the clip below, at least in the Key Lento area--which is the starting area of the game--it'll set you back $4.29 per gallon of unleaded, and $5.22 per gallon of diesel. Key Lento's real-world equivalent, Key West, currently has prices around $4.48 for unleaded and $6.11 for diesel--so it's technically cheaper to exist in Grand Theft Auto 6 right now. Of course, those prices should change as you progress through the different areas of Leonida, especially considering how Rockstar is aiming for a very realistic gameplay experience with GTA 6. We'll update this article with more prices when we spot them. For more on GTA 6, including how to steal cars, how to successfully commit robberies, and how to progress Jason and Lucia's romance, check out our GTA 6 guides hub.

title: GTA 6 Is Apparently Everything Rockstar Promised And Then Some
description: At long last, Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day has come. With Rockstar's latest project steadily unlocking as the clock strikes midnight worldwide, GTA 6 reviews have gone live, and the praise has been overwhelmingly positive so far. In fact, GTA 6 is reviewing so well that it's currently tied with the 1998 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated game of all time on GameSpot's sister site Metacritic, a feat that has taken 28 years to equal. So what are the reviewers saying? Amongst the flurry of perfect scores, a lot of the consensus is geared toward the world that Rockstar Games has created for its co-protagonists to inhabit, a sandbox that reacts to you in a variety of unique and interesting ways. It's a genre-defining experience for open-world games, as Rockstar has raised the bar to a tremendously high level for any other open-world game that'll follow in its footsteps. Here's what some reviewers have to say, and for more on the game, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub for an evolving collection of walkthroughs, tips, and tricks. Grand Theft Auto 6 Platforms: PS5 and Xbox Series X|S Price $80 for the Standard Edition, $100 for the Ultimate Edition Release date: November 19 GameSpot -- 10/10 Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realizing such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. title: The GTA 6 Map Is Truly, Truly Massive (Of Course)
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived--at least in New Zealand and Australia. Lots of people are playing the game already and have made a number of discoveries, including just how massive the map is. Even though we knew the GTA 6 map would be big--it has more playable space than GT4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined --seeing the map for yourself shows off its truly gargantuan scale. The streamer N3on showed off the entire GTA 6 map, and it's... large. As confirmed previously, GTA 6 takes place in the state of Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida. The central hub is Vice City itself (GTA's version of Miami), but the game takes players well beyond that to numerous surrounding counties. GTA 6 also carries the franchise's "fog of war" tradition forward, so that's why you don't see specific details on the map in N3on's video. As players find new places, they will show up more clearly on the map. But what's obvious at this point is that the GTA 6 map is gigantic. We can only wonder how long it may take to drive from one side to the other, or get all the way down to GTA 6's version of the Southernmost point in the continental US, Key West. GTA 6's version of the Florida Keys is called Leonida Keys. GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. “GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7,” reviewer Tamoor Hussain said. GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever. After GTA 6 reviews came online, shares of Rockstar owner Take-Two ripped higher, but the company is still down massively this year and over the past 12 months. title: The Nintendo GameCube Controller Was So Good That It Refuses To Die
description: The Nintendo GameCube is celebrating its 25-year anniversary on November 18, 2026. Below, we look back at its controller and why it's still considered an all-time great. There are myriad video game controllers we’ve come to hold dear over the years. Whether it be the reliable yet simplistic Xbox 360 pad, the charmingly petite DualShock 3, or the unique form factor offered by the Switch Joy-Con. Every single peripheral has its own distinct history, as they work hand in hand with the games we play and fall in love with. But I struggle to think of one with more of a legacy than the Nintendo GameCube controller. This thing is something special, and all because it had something to prove: to be better than everything that came before. As the console celebrates its 25th anniversary, I want to look back on what makes the purple pad so timeless, and why after all these years, it remains a constant in the gaming landscape. You might harbor plenty of nostalgia for the Nintendo 64 controller, but I refuse to believe it wasn’t invented specifically for an ancient race of underground spider people. Its protruding middle handle and single analogue stick meant it wasn’t especially comfortable to hold, and games like Super Mario 64 and GoldenEye did some truly magical things to play as well as they did considering the circumstances. Goldeneye 007 on N64 Regardless, it still made bold steps forward as the medium began to fully embrace the third dimension. But when compared to what the PS1 was offering with its innovative DualShock, it fell short. GameCube clawed back ground and then Nintendo introduced a design that, for whatever reason, hasn’t been replicated since. Fortunately, it stuck around and has become a mainstay for hardcore audiences. The GameCube controller, like any new console's controller, began by addressing the flaws of what came before. N64’s unintuitive trio of handles could eventually be mastered by most hardcore gamers, but newcomers would take one look at the…

Miami Heat player Myron Gardner posted a photo of the care package that arrived for him, which includes the aforementioned PS5 Pro console, two officially licensed GTA 6 DualSense controllers, and a physical copy of the game, all sealed in a padded case. Image credit: Myron Gardner on Instagram The consoles will likely be a small incentive for the Miami Heat team, as they'll be representing their city and GTA 6 when they hit the court tonight for a match against the Milwaukee Bucks. Developer Rockstar Games and publisher Take-Two Interactive have taken over the Miami Heat stadium, decking it out in custom GTA 6 graphics and insignia for the basketball game, as well as custom uniforms for the team. The Miami Heat are the odds-on favorites to win, as they've enjoyed a five-game winning streak lately, while the Milwaukee Bucks are looking to break their current losing streak, which is now 10 games long. The A Night in Vice City basketball game is set to be a big attraction, as it'll cap off the global rollout of GTA 6 tonight when the game unlocks in the US. Already active in several other time zones at the time of writing, GTA 6 has received overwhelmingly positive reviews and is the highest-rated game of the year. title: GTA 6 Owner Take-Two’s Stock Explodes After High Review Scores, But It’s Still Down Massively This Year
description: After more than 10 years of waiting, Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally available now (at least in New Zealand and Australia ). The anticipation has been sky-high for both consumers and investors alike, and Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, is seeing a huge uplift in its share price today after the game's overwhelmingly positive reviews landed. The US stock market doesn't officially open until 9:30 AM ET, but ahead of that, Take-Two shares are up close to 7% in pre-market trading. If this holds, it would boost Take-Two's total market cap by billions, and it could go even higher. Stock analysts expected share value to increase in the lead-up to launch, and many expect it to go higher still due to the expected launches of GTA Online and a PC edition of the game in 2027. While Take-Two's stock price is popping today, Take-Two remains down close to 20% so far in 2026 and is down about 15% over the past 12 months. Why? No one really knows, because the stock market is fickle. Take-Two's stock price got hammered earlier this year when Google announced new AI software to make games, presumably spooking investors. The stock has not recovered since. The 52-week high for Take-Two is $265.65, and the 52-week low is $183.86. Take-Two closed on November 17 at $203.93, but is up to $216 in pre-market trading today. As stated, the market opens at 9:30 AM ET today, so check back for more. GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. "GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," reviewer Tamoor Hussain said. GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever. title: GTA 6’s GTA+ Subscription Includes A Free Supercar, Discounts, And More
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is rolling out worldwide, and if you have a GTA+ subscription, you can pick up extra goodies for your trip to Vice City. Developer Rockstar Games has revealed that it'll be evolving its subscription service to cover both GTA Online and GTA 6, and for $8 a month, players can unlock several in-game benefits, including store discounts, more public transit options, and better haggling power. If you've preordered GTA 6, you'll automatically get a month of GTA+ for free. One thing to note: the services below are only available while you're subscribed, so if your membership expires or you cancel, those perks will no longer be available. Here's a breakdown of what you'll get if you stay subscribed. Venturas Blvd Elegy supercar and garage Looks do matter in Vice City, and nothing looks better than a '90 Annis Venturas BLVD Elegy supercar when you hit the streets. This high-speed vehicle can be safely stored in a single-car garage in Crosstown, which also includes a weapon locker and the ability to fence stolen items directly. You'll gain access to it after you complete Chapter 3 in GTA 6. Transit Service Bonuses If you'd prefer to rely on public transit, you can grab an upgrade for these facilities. This includes Scooter Bros Premium, premium membership on the RydeMe rideshare app, free scooter, bike, and Seashark rentals, and free rides on Leonida public transportation. Store discounts Select businesses across the city will also offer you a 10% discount on their services. Weapons and clothes shops, hairdressers, tattooists, vehicle mod shops, and more are included. Increased sell value Selling an eligible vehicle will also net you an extra 10% in cash. Meanwhile, GTA Online players are also getting plenty of bang for their buck with GTA+ this month, as they can unlock a free car, in-game discounts, the Vinewood Car Club features, bonuses, and more. title: GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, off its throne? The answer is a resounding yes: not only is GTA 6 being reviewed higher than Nintendo's little hero in green, but it's also emerging as one of the highest-rated games of all time. When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 147 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score. GTA 6 is only the second game to earn a metascore of 98, and hilariously, it's tied with the original Ocarina of Time from 1998. Historically, GTA games have always had some of the highest review aggregates, especially after the series moved to the third dimension. Starting with GTA 3, mainline entries have all earned metascores in the high 90s, with Grand Theft Auto 4 being the highest-reviewed game in the franchise until GTA 6 came along. Here's a closer look at those metascores over the years.: Grand Theft Auto — No metascore Grand Theft Auto 2 — 70 Grand Theft Auto 3 — 97 Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — 95 Grand Theft Auto 4 — 98 Grand Theft Auto 5 — 97 Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud…

title: How Long To Beat GTA 6 – Full Missions List
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally in our grubby little hands, and after years (and years) of waiting, we've finished it. If you're just about to get into the game, you might be wondering just how much of a time sink it's going to be. While we recommend taking your time and exploring all of Leonida at your own pace, as games media we didn't quite have that luxury. The benefit for you is that we can give you a pretty good recommendation of how many hours you can expect it to take to complete GTA 6's main story. To finish GTA 6, you can expect to spend anywhere upwards of 65 hours on the main campaign. Some of our staff spent more time exploring the side missions and other activities, clocking in at 90-100 hours. However, so far no-one on the GameSpot team has completed 100% of the game--we're only human, after all. From our estimations, to do that you're looking at upwards of 200 hours. There's a serious shedload of content. All GTA 6 Missions There are a staggering amount of main missions in the GTA 6 story, and we've listed them all below.
